findings.title: Reuse the existing plant-comparison answer in plant science
findings.detail: All 35 Soil and Plant Scientist candidates already have a positive frozen plant-comparison answer. The six-item bank connects that answer only to Biological Technician. It can support the plant-comparison method in its own stated scope; reporting and advice remain separate.
findings.guard: One model, grok075-0705, is missing only this method check. This is one especially clear closure candidate, not 35 guaranteed new Tops. Seventeen of the 35 dislike the distinct sample-preparation item; preserve those answers.

findings.title: Separate childcare from medical patient care
findings.detail: The two Childcare Worker bindings require r:patientcare, whose actual statement concerns direct medical patient care. These 32 models explicitly select child-focused activities. The medical preference is not the child-care responsibility being asked.
findings.guard: Replace the clinical proxy with child-care-specific routines and safeguarding evidence. Ask where that evidence is missing; do not automatically promote every tutor or game helper.

findings.title: Offer animal care without turning it into animal research
findings.detail: All 62 have Animal Scientist as a candidate, and 32 have no other candidate at all. The 457-career inventory lacks Animal Caretakers and Veterinary Assistants. Many narratives describe chosen kennel, feeding or routine care activities, not research.
findings.guard: Add appropriate care roles with their own scoped questions and verified training/pay data. Keep animal-production research and clinical interests unknown unless separately answered.

findings.title: Check contextual technical evidence before demanding another generic tag
findings.detail: These 24 models have Electronics Engineer or Computer Programmer candidates. Their selected activity statements already describe tracing a failed connection or program and testing changes. Some remaining method bindings demand additional generic design, investigation or precision preferences.
findings.guard: Use exact activity-specific implications only where the target question asks the same thing. Requirements gathering, safety, documentation and communication still need their own evidence. Twenty-four is a review population, not a predicted lift.

findings.title: Allow document and interview research without mandatory statistics
findings.detail: Political Scientist and Anthropologist/Archeologist candidates include qualitative routes, but their baseline method bindings respectively require quantitative or outdoor-fieldwork preferences. A systematic document/interview route needs its own correctly scoped alternative.
findings.guard: Systematic inquiry, subject context and explaining uncertainty remain necessary. Broad policy or history enthusiasm is not a complete research match.

findings.title: Keep earth interest distinct from extraction and boundary work
findings.detail: These 31 profiles select rocks, terrain maps and runoff comparisons. That single activity gives domain support to surveying, mining and petroleum candidates. It does not establish interest in legal boundaries or extracting resources.
findings.guard: Add context branches before loosening technical methods. This can reduce weak invitations; it should not be sold as a Top-coverage increase.

findings.title: Distinguish writing a mathematical argument from teaching
findings.detail: Ten models have Mathematician candidates; seven are missing only the responsibility check. The general explaining method is phrased as finding a second example when someone is confused. That is narrower and more teaching-oriented than making reasoning checkable.
findings.guard: Ask about sharing written assumptions and reasoning. Do not override explicit dislike of explaining or assume a new interest merely from liking puzzles.

findings.title: Separate direct learner support, course assessment and educator coaching
findings.detail: Thirty-one models have Instructional Coordinator candidates based on learning-guide interests. Coaching educators and making course-level decisions remain different activities. Some would prefer direct help with learners.
findings.guard: Keep educator-coaching and assessment checks where relevant. Add teaching-assistant and other direct-support options before steering a student into administration.

findings.title: Ask about the actual edit rather than broad precision
findings.detail: Fourteen Film and Video Editor candidates are missing the second defining interest. A general precision preference is not identical to comparing picture, sound and timing. Existing movie-editing answers can anchor a concrete follow-up.
findings.guard: Retain the unresolved production component; do not treat watching clips, generic creativity or appearing on camera as editing confirmation.

findings.title: Wire the existing safety follow-up to practical routes too
findings.detail: Eleven wood-interested models leave safety responsibility unknown. Carpenter questions require it, while the existing safety bridge targets engineering and architecture rather than carpentry.
findings.guard: Offer the same supervised safety choice in the relevant practical context. Preserve unknown or negative answers; do not infer tool-safety interest from skill or family work.
